correctness.rationale: For every \(q\ge3\) and \(k\ge0\), decomposition into length-\(L\) substitution blocks shows no adjacent 1-blocks and identifies five exhaustive and pairwise disjoint length-\(2L\) factor families; the 101 family occurs if and only if \(q=3\). The two full-weight families alone have \(T=2^k\) ones, while every proper block segment has fewer. Complete-set enumeration independently agrees for 24 finite parameter pairs; finite tests are not used as the infinite proof.

evidence: Lü et al., 2015 online, Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 identify right-special factors and total factor complexity, not maximum-weight factor words.
Chen et al., 2017, Lemma 2 bounds the number of ones but does not enumerate the maximizing factors.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader factor-complexity knowledge encompasses every factor numerically but does not encode a Parikh-fiber classification. A known value of the maximum among factors is strictly weaker than the exact set and multiplicity of all maximizers; the \(q\ge4\) parameter transition is also outside the later ordinary-Cantor-only lemma.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The \(q=3\) maximum value \(T=2^k\) is explicitly prior-covered. Published factor-count formulas \(4L-1\) or \(3L\) agree with, but do not logically determine, the extreme fiber cardinality \(2L\) or \(L+1\); many distributions of one-counts can have the same total and same maximum. The disjoint family proof is needed to obtain the new statement.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The published total-factor table is explicitly identified as prior art, not claimed new. The sharp maximum-fiber cardinality and full word-level classification were not found in the inspected sources; unsuccessful searches alone do not establish novelty.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons separate the already-known total factor complexity and ordinary-Cantor maximum weight from the new exact maximum-weight fiber and its \(q=3\) versus \(q\ge4\) multiplicity transition. Targeted searches for extremal Parikh class size, densest windows, and weight-maximizing factors did not uncover a dominating result. A still-unindexed equivalent classification remains possible.
residual_risks: The extremal-fiber classification may appear in other unindexed work on Cantor-like sequences or follow from an uninspected specialized theorem; no claim of exhaustive global literature uniqueness is made.

value.rationale: The extreme Parikh-fiber is a natural word-reconstruction/abelian-spectrum statistic not determined by the published factor-count or maximum-weight functions. The proof identifies every maximizing word at every substitution depth in an infinite parameter family, exhibiting a sharp parameter transition: \(2L\) extremizers (half of all distinct factors asymptotically) when \(q=3\) versus \(L+1\) (one-third asymptotically) when \(q\ge4\). The central 101 block pattern gives a structural, not numerical, explanation.
